key_insight: AgentSSL frames semi-supervised learning as a program search problem, asking whether automated ML engineering agents can make effective use of abundant unlabeled data when labels are scarce. The provided abstract is incomplete, so it does not establish performance gains.
problem_solved: ML engineering agents have largely been studied in fully supervised settings, leaving their ability to build pipelines for label-scarce, unlabeled-data-rich domains untested.
method: Introduce Agentic Semi-Supervised Learning (AgentSSL) as a setting for automated ML engineering.
Frame semi-supervised learning pipeline development as a program search problem.
Investigate whether MLE agents can leverage unlabeled data alongside limited labeled examples.
impact: This work targets two practical bottlenecks: acquiring labels and manually engineering ML pipelines. Effective agents in this setting could reduce the effort needed to adapt ML systems to new domains, though the supplied excerpt does not report results.
visual_elements: Data-pool graphic contrasting a small labeled set with a large unlabeled set.
Workflow diagram: labeled and unlabeled data → MLE agent → candidate learning pipelines.
Search-tree illustration showing semi-supervised pipeline development as program search.
Side-by-side schematic contrasting fully supervised and semi-supervised agent settings.
paper_title: AgentSSL: Can MLE Agents Leverage Unlabeled Data?
paper_authors: Ethan Lin, Akanksha Sarkar, Ziang Liu, Kristin Branson, Jennifer J. Sun
